llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says, but it gives agents broad publishing, Drive storage, sharing-token, and persistent credential authority that deserves review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network access to here.now and Cloudflare R2 plus local file uploads are expected for publishing/storage, but the helpers can transmit arbitrary selected local files and import/export folder trees, so user-controlled path selection is important.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The install examples use an unpinned global npx install and the skill directs agents to trust live docs/API behavior, creating normal supply-chain and behavior-drift risk rather than artifact-backed malice.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Several operations are scoped by user intent, but the skill uses broad triggers such as sharing or generating a URL, instructs agents to save API keys without an explicit consent checkpoint, and the Drive share helper can create write-capable tokens with broad scope if not carefully parameterized.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists API keys in ~/.herenow/credentials and publish state in .herenow/state.json; the state file is purpose-aligned, but automatic long-lived credential storage without asking is overbroad.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently support here.now publishing and storage, but the top description emphasizes publishing while the body and bundled scripts also expose private Drive read/write/delete, import/export, and share-token management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if you use shared machines or sensitive files. Only use it when you are comfortable letting the agent upload chosen local files to here.now/R2, publish public or access-controlled sites, manage private Drive contents, create sharing tokens, and store a here.now API key under ~/.herenow/credentials. Ask the agent to confirm exact paths, destination, visibility, token permissions, path prefix, TTL, and credential storage before it acts.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Drive storage is documented in the body and scripts, but it is broader than the headline publishing description, so this is partially supported as under-disclosure rather than hidden behavior.
[TM1] expected: Folder create/rename/delete capabilities are account-mutating but are disclosed, and the text says not to invent folders or file Sites unless the user asks.
[LP3] expected: Shell, curl, local files, credentials, and network access are necessary for this hosting/storage helper, but the artifact would benefit from tighter declared permission boundaries.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Broad invocation phrases could cause accidental uploads for vague sharing requests, so this concern is accepted as a scoping issue.
[RA2] expected: No cron, service, startup hook, or backdoor persistence was found; the artifact uses ordinary credential and state files for the service.
[RP1] unexpected: The unpinned npx install examples are real supply-chain drift risk, though not evidence of malicious behavior in the inspected artifact.
[EA2] unexpected: The stale-base workflow is user-protective, but the instruction to save returned API keys immediately without asking is a material consent concern.
[PE2] expected: The chmod 600 command restricts credential-file permissions and does not use sudo or root privileges, so this finding is downgraded.
[E1] expected: External transmission to here.now and returned upload URLs is expected for publishing and Drive storage, but users should approve what local files and email addresses are sent.
[P4] expected: The referenced user-output instructions are operational guidance for presenting claim URLs and avoiding misleading state-file references, not prompt injection.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The Drive script is fully present and documented in the body, but it materially expands the skill beyond the initial publish-focused description.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Share-token creation is purpose-aligned for agent handoff, but write tokens, optional token-management rights, broad path prefixes, and no default TTL create a real overbreadth concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Direct uploads of local file contents are inherent to publishing and Drive import, but should be surfaced clearly to the user before execution.
